Hi Alice — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the open items we promised to follow up on: 

1) PII scope: you mentioned customer names, payment tokens, and free-text support transcripts; you also called out a small set of internal IDs used for matching. Can you confirm whether the payment token is stored raw or is always hashed before it reaches any SaaS endpoints? (I left a stub spreadsheet attached to record exact fields)

2) Retention policy: you said legal requires 12 months for transcripts but security is pushing for 90 days for anything that contains sensitive fields — we need a clear policy so we can confirm default retention + per-customer overrides.

3) Logging & audit: please confirm whether you need request/response payloads in access logs, or just metadata (request id, timestamp, model/version). If payloads are required, are they allowed to be stored in-region only?

4) Network boundaries & egress: clarify whether you need an air-gapped (no internet) on-prem deployment, or VPC-connected with strict egress to specific S3 buckets and internal endpoints. You also raised concerns about KV cache residency — we can pin cache to the VPC.

Olga — thanks, that summary is helpful. Quick clarifications inline: 

1) Payment tokens: our payments platform currently issues tokenized identifiers and we only persist the token (no PAN). Tokens are considered sensitive and legal prefers hashing at rest; we can provide a note from payments if necessary.

2) Retention: legal will accept 12 months for transcripts if we can ensure PII fields are redacted after 90 days. Is field-level redaction something Redwood supports server-side, or would that require an extractor before ingestion?

3) Logging: security wants metadata in logs and an option to store request/response payloads for 30 days max for auditability. Any payload storage must be locked to our us-west-2 region.

4) Network: primary preference is VPC deployment with no internet egress except to our internal S3 endpoint and to our internal model registry during sync windows. We may evaluate an air-gapped on-prem option for a small pilot. We also want guarantees that KV caches and prefix caches can be pinned to our VPC and not replicated externally.

I’ve attached the security contact (security@fintegral.com) and our infra lead Paul to review the network asks. I’ll fill out the PII spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.

— Alice

Quick answers (technical):

- Field-level redaction: we have two viable approaches. Option A: server-side redaction hooks in the ingestion pipeline (configurable field patterns + regex) — minimal infra changes but adds CPU overhead during ingest. Option B: pre-ingest transformer (recommended for heavy throughput) — customer runs a lightweight agent to redact/mask before requests hit our endpoints. Both support redaction+hashing workflows.

- KV cache residency: we can pin KV caches to the customer VPC with node affinity. That prevents cross-VPC replication; however, durability across failures would rely on a single-customer replica set inside the VPC. If they require multi-AZ durability, we can keep replicas but still restrict them to the same region/account.

- Model registry sync / egress: we support scheduled sync windows and explicit allow-lists for destination IPs and S3 endpoints. For strict egress constraints, we can provide a hardened NAT + egress proxy that only permits outbound traffic to listed endpoints and logs flows.

- Logs & retention: default application logs include metadata only. We can enable payload logging as an opt-in feature and configure TTLs per customer; payload logs stored in-region only. For audit evidence, we can export redacted payload bundles to a customer-controlled S3 bucket.

Attachments: rfi_network_diagram.pdf (network diagram showing VPC peering and egress proxy)

I’ll prepare a short ops checklist for the architecture call: pinning KV cache, sync windows, NAT/egress proxy config, retention TTLs, required access for our operators for troubleshooting (time-limited).

— Rishi
